We have a 10 year old Whirlpool washer that would "not" spin at times. Because it would spin and work just fine sometimes I was thinking the problem was inside the transmission. I ordered a coupling, a clutch kit and the neutral drain kit. I figured if I had the transmission out and the problem was not the coupling or the clutch I wanted to proceed to rebuilding the transmission and have the parts on hand. After removing the pump, motor, and then the transmission I determined the coupling was good but I had a new one so I replaced it. I then determined the clutch was warn/bad/lose/slipping. I installed the 285785 clutch kit, all the parts fit perfectly. I reinstalled everything and ran the washer through 15 loads of wash so far, some heavy some light, it works like new. We had not noticed that it was spinning slower (when it did spin) and now with the new clutch the wash is drying much faster as more water is being removed.

I don't care for the "new" (HE) washers as on most you do not have the choices I have with my old one. Bottom line, instead of spending five to seven hundred dollars for a new washer I repaired my old one for under $35.00. The $20.00 dollar neutral spin kit I did not use I'll keep for now.

This is the third type of reusable k-cup coffee filter that I've tried, and frankly, it was going to be the last, since I've been less than impressed by the functioning of the others tried.  These, however, are the best attempt to date that I've added to my Keurig single brew 'custom' option.  Firstly, you get four of them, so if you want several cups of coffee, you don't have to worry about cleaning the last one out, just grab another one.  Secondly, there's only one part in all, since the lid is attached to the body of the coffee filter.  So, easy to keep track of.  Thirdly, they work pretty well.  the key is not to fill them more than 1/4" from the top of the basket, and they shouldn't pour their guts out all over the machine like some others do, putting grinds into your coffee and around the coffee maker's innards as well.  They work best in my low level Keurig machine if only brewing at the mid size, or 8 oz. size cup I believe it is.  Easy to clean out, they are the best design and manufactured product of this type available out there.  Trust me.
